History:
• 53-year-old man presents with new swelling over the left elbow, first noticed ~1 week ago while showering.  
• Swelling is largely painless; only mild “weird” sensation and slight tenderness adjacent to tip.  
• Elbow feels slightly warm compared with surrounding skin; no marked redness, no limitation of movement, no systemic symptoms (fever, malaise).  
• Denies trauma or repetitive strain; works a desk job. No prior episodes.  
• No family history of rheumatoid arthritis or lupus recalled.  

Past Medical History:
• Osteoarthritis – GP-diagnosed several years ago.  
• Allergy: peanuts (food). Denies medication allergies.  
• Medications: none routinely (started OTC ibuprofen today—400 mg dose/route/frequency not documented, but plan provided).  
• Otherwise healthy; runs 2–3×/week.  

Physical Examination:
• General: Appears well on video; alert and oriented.  
• Left elbow: Visible focal swelling over olecranon bursa; overlying skin slightly warm and minimally tender lateral to tip; skin at tip noted dry. Full active range of motion. No obvious erythema, no visible skin breach.  
• Other systems: Not recorded. Vitals: Not recorded.  

Impression:
Likely aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis of the left elbow.  
Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript:  
1. Aseptic olecranon bursitis – classic painless swelling with minor warmth, preserved motion.  
2. Septic olecranon bursitis – less likely; monitor for increasing pain, redness, systemic features.  
3. Gouty bursitis – consider; blood work ordered to evaluate urate level.  

Management Plan:
• Pharmacologic: Commence ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily after food; discontinue if heartburn occurs.  
• Investigations: Mail‐out pathology forms for CBC, CRP/ESR, rheumatologic antibodies, serum urate and infection screen.  
• Follow-up: Review via video or face-to-face after blood results (~6 days post-draw).  
• Red-flag advice: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, warmth spreads, or systemic symptoms develop (concern for septic arthritis/bursitis).  
• Documentation: Arrange paperwork mailing and schedule follow-up appointment on patient request after labs.  

Patient Summary:
A healthy 53-year-old man developed a painless, mildly warm swelling over the left olecranon one week ago. Clinical picture is most consistent with aseptic bursitis; anti-inflammatory therapy and blood tests have been arranged, with safety-netting for possible infection.  

Key Takeaways:
• Take ibuprofen 400 mg with food twice daily for inflammation; stop if stomach upset.  
• Obtain ordered blood tests promptly; arrange follow-up once results are available.  
• If swelling becomes red, very painful, or spreads, contact GP at Hand or seek urgent care immediately.  

Next Steps:
• Patient to complete blood tests within the next few days.  
• Provider to review results and reassess elbow in ~1 week.  
• Consider further imaging or aspiration if symptoms worsen or blood work suggests infection or gout.
